prompt: Models are fitted on 1990–2014 and judged on 2015–2026, a period they never saw.
why: Out-of-sample evaluation measures forecasting, not curve fitting.
trap: AIC judges in-sample; this judges the future.

prompt: Each day's forecast uses only returns up to the previous day, and parameters are never updated during the test.
tells: only returns up to the previous day
why: Preventing look-ahead makes the test honest.
trap: Using any future data would flatter the model.

prompt: Besides VaR breaches, you score each model by the log-likelihood of the 2015–2026 returns under its frozen parameters.
why: Out-of-sample log-likelihood judges the whole forecast distribution, not just the 1% tail.
trap: It reuses the likelihood, but as an evaluation score.

prompt: The paper compares GARCH models against a rolling 250-day volatility and RiskMetrics EWMA, which have no fitted parameters.
why: Simple benchmarks show whether fitting a model adds value over cheap rules.
trap: EWMA is IGARCH, but here it plays the benchmark role.

prompt: A model with three extra parameters wins easily in-sample but has a worse log-likelihood than plain GARCH on the test period.
tells: worse log-likelihood than plain GARCH on the test period
why: In-sample gains that vanish out of sample signal overfitting.
trap: AIC might have warned, but the test-period result decides.

prompt: Parameters fitted on 1990–2014 are used unchanged through 2026, so any drift in market behavior goes unmodeled.
why: A fixed-window design is a limitation; rolling or expanding re-estimation is the usual remedy.
trap: Simple and honest, but it assumes stable parameters.
